newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonds ended down on Friday for the third day in a row, but traders said bonos had at least stopped underperforming other debt markets.
The 10-year spread over Bunds closed at 93 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close, but below the 97 basis points reached this morning.
"The spread trend is proving the Spanish correction should be almost over," a dealer said adding, that Bonos will likely track other markets.
Dealers said they had been eyeing U.S. markets, where treasuries were mostly down at midday.
A weaker peseta, trading at around 84.31/34 against the mark, from 84.07/09 at yesterday's close, cooled expectations for a quick cut in the official interest rate.
This helped flatten the yield curve, the spread between the two- and ten-year bonds declining to 139 basis points from 143 basis points.
